archive-length-in-the-size-mismatch-warn: The warning for a wrong-length download reads `archive size <got> does not match the pinned <pinned>`, and the lengths are those of a gzip level 9 archive, which depend on the zlib build. The golden holds `archive size <A> does not match the pinned <A+1>` (the pinned length is one more than the fetched one); the replay substitutes the fetched length for <A>.
maxBytes-is-recorded-relative-to-the-pin: The fetch is handed maxBytes equal to the pinned archive size. The golden records `maxBytesMinusPinnedArchive` (0, or 1 for the size-plus-one pin) rather than the number, for the same zlib reason as above.
fs-error-prefix: verifyInstalledOverlay answers err.message for an error it catches. Under jest an fs error comes from outside the test realm, so `instanceof Error` is false and the module prints `Error: ENOENT: ...`; in the app it prints `ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '<path>'`. The golden holds the app's text (the `Error: ` prefix removed). The Rust replay maps ENOENT to the platform's not-found text and compares the rest.
env-failure-text: `overlay env failed: Error: boom; launching without it` is String(err) of a scripted rejection. The replay's scripted installer fails with the same message and the module formats `Error: <message>`.
hostile-archive-as-found: knownFixOverlayInstall--ensureoverlayinstalled-refuses-a-hostile-archive-whose-sha-matches-the-pin is recorded as the TS test builds it: its header has no ustar magic, so the refusal is `not a POSIX ustar entry` and not the path check. outcome-hostile-archive-with-a-real-dotdot-entry is the same attack with a well-formed header (`".." path segment: ../x`). See .planning/todos/pending/2026-11-25-overlay-install-hostile-archive-test-fails-on-the-magic-not-the-dotdot-name.md.
concurrent-fetch-order: When two boots install at once their fetches are listed by boot (A then B), not in the order the file system checks happened to finish.
tree-names-are-fixed: tree.json lists the whole fake HOME afterwards. Temporary names (`.<id>.partial-*`, `.<id>.stale-*`) never survive an install, which `leftovers: []` proves, so no random name is in a golden.
